title: AppState (signals store)
before:
Title: AppState (signals store)
Kind: store
Links: external-references, ghost-branches, graph-model, node-history, project-files, rules-model, workbench-files
Files:
  src/state.rs
  src/config.rs

Central reactive store made of Dioxus signals: graph, baseline, rules, related GitHub repos, the MCP connections and their last reported status, the user's provider settings, the projects list and whether the project view is showing, selection, the module scope path (which network the graph view shows), chat items, session id, model, cost, the chat mode and a plan waiting for approval, open file, tabs and the active job.
It also holds the domain actions: open/save/revert files, load and sync the workbench from disk, update and save the graph or the current network, enter and leave modules, compute changes against the baseline, revert node and module changes, mark the graph as in sync, and update rules, related repos and MCP connections (saving MCP connections restarts Workbench on the next message).
For plain chat turns it snapshots the graph when the turn starts and, when the turn succeeds, moves the graph edits Workbench made into the baseline (the whole graph if it was in sync, otherwise only Workbench's changes), so they don't show up as the user's pending changes.
Edits the user makes in the graph during the turn stay pending.
Also defines the Cmd enum sent to the session loop.

author: KarlOlofA
title: Workbench session loop
before:
Title: Workbench session loop
Kind: service
Links: agent-layer, app-state, mcp-connections, prompt-builder
Files:
  src/session.rs
  src/history.rs

Long-running coroutine that receives Cmd values (Send, Prompt, Interrupt, Restart) and owns the live agent.
With Workbench it spawns the agent process lazily, respawns it when the rules version changes, and resumes the stored session id.
A generation counter drops events from killed processes.
Streamed events become chat items; file-touching tool results bump repo_version and reload the open file, and Done finishes the current graph job.
Every delivered message outside a job starts a chat turn in app-state, which Done settles against the baseline.
Changing a project's repositories or descriptions also restarts Workbench with the updated project context.
When it spawns the agent it passes the enabled MCP connections as --mcp-config, and the MCP statuses from the agent's init event go to app-state.
With any other provider every message starts a new turn through the agent layer, and only Workbench sessions are remembered for the session history.
after:
Title: Workbench session loop
Kind: service
Links: agent-layer, app-state, chat-sessions, mcp-connections, prompt-builder
Files:
  src/session.rs
  src/history.rs

One long-running loop per agent that receives that agent's Cmd values (Send, Prompt, Interrupt, Restart, Resume) and owns its live agent, so agents in a session work at the same time.
With Workbench it spawns the agent process lazily in the agent's folder, respawns it when the rules version changes, and resumes the agent's stored session id.
A generation counter drops events from killed processes.
Streamed events become the agent's chat items; when the agent works in the open folder, file-touching tool results bump repo_version and reload the open file, and Done settles its chat turn or graph job against the baseline.
A reply that ends with spawn-agent blocks starts those agents in the same session with their tasks.
Changing a project's repositories or descriptions also restarts Workbench with the updated project context.
When it spawns the agent it passes the enabled MCP connections as --mcp-config, and the MCP statuses from the agent's init event go to app-state.
With any other provider every message starts a new turn through the agent layer, and only Workbench session ids are saved for resuming.

Chat sessions, each bound to one folder (a repository checkout or a worktree) and holding one or more agents.
Each agent is its own conversation with its own agent process and session loop; its live state (messages, busy, queued messages, permissions, plan, mode, model, cost, input) is a Chat in app-state.
Sessions, agent names and each agent's provider session id are saved in ~/.config/workbench/chat_sessions.json, so the conversations resume after a restart; a folder's first session resumes the conversation it had before sessions existed.

Changing a project's repositories or descriptions also restarts Workbench with the updated project context.

Title: Claims (branch work overlap)
Kind: service
Links: ghost-branches, git-service, graph-model
Files:

Derives the blast radius of intent work from git, without storing anything: the nodes a graph diff changes, the files those nodes own, and the nodes that link to them.
open_claims reads every other branch with commits HEAD doesn't have, and builds each branch's claim from its graph diffed against the merge base plus the code files it changed, together with the branch's authors.
overlaps compares the local pending changes with those claims, so contention shows up before any agent runs.

Shown instead of the graph while .workbench/graph.json has an unresolved git merge conflict.
It merges the three merge stages per node: intent changed on one side only is taken as is, and a node or module whose intent both sides changed differently is listed as a conflict with both versions side by side (description, links, files) and the nodes that use it.
